competences: The learner identifies sourced facts about responsibilities of a citizen.
The learner explains information relating to Responsibilities of a citizen in developing Uganda.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads and spells: responsibilities, citizen, duties, development.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to state facts about responsibilities of a citizen.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer original sourced questions on Responsibilities of a citizen in developing Uganda.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied related ideas about Uganda and its population or government. They use this knowledge in studying responsibilities of a citizen.
materials: Reference chart about responsibilities of a citizen
P5 SST notes about Responsibilities of a citizen in developing Uganda
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher asks learners to recall earlier Social Studies work and introduces responsibilities of a citizen. They ask the original question "State any four responsibilities of a good citizen in Uganda." and note the learners' responses before teaching the content.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous work, answer the opening question and explain what they already know about Uganda and its people.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about responsibilities of a citizen
steps.content: Briefly give the meaning of a citizen Point out two ways one can become a citizen of Uganda. By denouncing the citizenship. Responsibilities/duties/obligations of a citizen To protect the citizens and their property through the army. To provide social services like education to the citizens. Keeps law and order. Pays tax promptly Preserves his environment Respects and preserves the rights and freedom of others
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Meaning and key facts about responsibilities of a citizen", starting with "Briefly give the meaning of a citizen; Point out two ways one can become a citizen of Uganda.". They explain the information, clarify the meanings and check learners' understanding through questioning.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source notes, explain the main points, answer their teacher's questions and copy the factual information into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about responsibilities of a citizen
steps.content: Upholds the national constitution Respects the nation’s attributes. Renders national services whenever they are required. Participates in the national activities which promote democracy and good governance e.g. general elections Participate in self help projects. Activity To provide and guide development programme to all areas of the country. Citizenship by birth A person born by parents who are Ugandans becomes a citizen of Uganda by birth. Citizenship by registration
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Features and related facts about responsibilities of a citizen", starting with "Upholds the national constitution; Respects the nation’s attributes.". They explain the information, clarify the meanings and check learners' understanding through questioning.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source notes, explain the main points, answer their teacher's questions and copy the factual information into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further details about responsibilities of a citizen
steps.content: A person married to a Uganda citizen for at least a period of three years. Citizenship by Naturalization This is where a person from another country is made a citizen of a specified country after spending many years (20years) Citizenship by descent Right to access public information Responsibilities of citizens Define the following If a person becomes a citizen of another country To respect the rights of other citizens Through descent (is the legal right of belonging to a country a person gets when his / her ancestors were citizens in that country) Single citizenship. This is the legal right of belonging to one particular country.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Further details about responsibilities of a citizen", starting with "A person married to a Uganda citizen for at least a period of three years.; Citizenship by Naturalization". They explain the information, clarify the meanings and check learners' understanding through questioning.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source notes, explain the main points, answer their teacher's questions and copy the factual information into their books.

steps.content: State any four responsibilities of a good citizen in Uganda. | Define dual citizenship | How can one lose his chance of being a citizen of Uganda? | What do you understand by the term patriotism? | Who is a good citizen?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents the exact sourced questions, beginning with "State any four responsibilities of a good citizen in Uganda." and "Define dual citizenship". They supervise the written responses, check the answers against the lesson notes and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the questions in their books, compare their work with the factual notes and correct wrong or incomplete answers.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the important facts about responsibilities of a citizen and evaluates learning using "State any four responsibilities of a good citizen in Uganda." and "Define dual citizenship". They give guidance on the remaining original exercise for home revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer final oral questions, mention one important fact and make corrections in their notebooks before the lesson ends.

assessment: Use the original questions "State any four responsibilities of a good citizen in Uganda." and "Define dual citizenship" and other exercises to test understanding. Mark answers and assist pupils to correct them using the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining original sourced exercise questions, especially "How one can become a citizen of Uganda?"
